author: Buckeye Reporter
title: City Commission recognizes Regina Blackshear on retirement after five years of service
text:
The City Commission recognized the retirement of Clerk of Commission Regina Blackshear on Apr. 22 by declaring the day “Regina Blackshear Day.” Blackshear served in her role for more than five years, helping to ensure that commission meetings, operations, records, and other essential functions ran smoothly and in accordance with the City Charter and regulations. She also worked as office manager and paralegal in the Department of Law during her career with the City of Dayton.
Blackshear’s contributions were acknowledged as important to maintaining efficient city government processes. The recognition reflects a broader commitment by Dayton to support community engagement through boards, commissions, and public meetings while emphasizing transparency with accessible agendas, minutes, and government records, according to the official website .
Dayton provides municipal services through departments focused on public safety, public works, recreation, and economic development according to its official website . The city operates under a council-manager form of government with an elected mayor and city commission who appoint a professional city manager according to its official website .
In addition to honoring long-serving employees like Blackshear, Dayton is known for preserving its history as the birthplace of aviation and honoring figures such as the Wright brothers according to its official website . The city’s efforts include historic preservation at sites like the Wright Brothers’ bicycle shop and participation in national heritage initiatives according to its official website .
Dayton also promotes economic vitality through partnerships and development projects designed to strengthen local opportunities according to its official website . As Regina Blackshear retires from her position at City Hall—often referred to as “City Hall’s ‘sophisticated lady'”—the city continues its focus on effective governance and community involvement.
